assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration correction in electron optics is a genuine invention that opened a door: it moved routine transmission electron microscopy from the nanometre to the sub-angstrom regime, so atoms, interfaces and defects in oxides, catalysts and 2D materials can be seen and quantified directly. The principle (a multipole corrector for spherical aberration) had been judged impossible for decades, and its realization is a clear, original, instrument-level achievement with a very large downstream record. I note my own field and weigh this carefully against any appearance of favouritism, but on the criteria of invention, verification and impact it stands on its own.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the theoretical corrector design, Haider the engineering and construction of the hexapole corrector for the TEM, and Urban the first demonstration and application of the corrected instrument to materials. This is a coherent three-person configuration. The supplied credit does not include the independent STEM-corrector work led by Krivanek and collaborators, which is a real attribution question in this area.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed: corrected instruments are now standard worldwide and independently reproduced by several manufacturers and laboratories for over two decades. The invention is mature and recognition is, if anything, overdue.
uncertainties: Parallel STEM spherical-aberration correction (Krivanek and colleagues) is outside the supplied credited names and may need to be weighed; I cannot independently verify exact priority dates.
Whether the committee views this as physics rather than instrumentation or chemistry/materials science.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2018 observation of correlated insulating states and superconductivity near the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene, following the Bistritzer-MacDonald prediction of flat bands, opened moire quantum matter as a tunable platform. It combines a clear theoretical prediction with an original experiment, and a new class of materials where interaction physics can be dialled in by a twist angle. The importance and originality are high.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the 2011 flat-band prediction at the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group performed the original experiments (with Cao and co-workers, whose junior status raises a fairness concern under the three-person limit). The three-name configuration is defensible but does not cover all decisive experimental contributors, and the credit for the first experimental claim is partly with students and postdocs.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced independently by many groups, with a very large follow-on literature; the superconducting and correlated phase interpretation is still evolving, so some details are not settled, but the discovery itself is solid.
uncertainties: The microscopic origin of the superconductivity remains debated.
Credit to early-career experimentalists and to other theorists is not captured by three names.
Reproducibility and sample-to-sample variation in twist angle are known issues.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 2008 discovery of superconductivity in iron pnictides (LaFeAsO with fluorine doping, Tc about 26 K) was an unexpected, original experimental discovery that created a second family of high-temperature superconductors after the cuprates. It is exactly the type of discovery-driven result the prize is meant for: a surprising observation, quickly verified by many laboratories.
assessment.attribution: The decisive original discovery is attributable to Hosono and his group (Kamihara et al.). Chen and Zhao contributed the rapid increase of Tc above 40-55 K in related compounds, which is an important follow-up but not the original discovery; I would give priority to the first observation and propose Hosono alone as the cleanest attribution.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly replicated worldwide within weeks, and the family is well established; however, the mechanism of pairing is not settled and no technology has yet resulted, which could be argued to be premature for impact on humanity.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism remains unresolved.
Allocation between the original discovery and the Tc-enhancement follow-up may be contested by the committee.
Practical impact is limited so far.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy centres in diamond turned a point defect into a room-temperature quantum system that can be initialised, manipulated and read out, and underpins nanoscale magnetometry, thermometry and biological sensing. This is a new tool that lets people see things not accessible before, and it was experimentally demonstrated with clear original measurements.
assessment.attribution: Wrachtrup's group first detected single NV centres optically (1997) and demonstrated optically detected magnetic resonance on single spins; Jelezko made the key demonstrations of coherent control and coupling to nearby nuclear spins. Lukin and others made major contributions to sensing protocols and registers, and Awschalom, Hanson and others also contributed to spin control, so credit is shared across a larger community; I limit the proposal to the two foundational experimenters.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature technically with many independent confirmations and commercial instruments in preparation; the field is broad and still evolving, which makes the choice of a single moment harder.
uncertainties: Sensing field has many contributors beyond the supplied names.
Boundary between quantum information and sensing contributions is unclear.
I cannot verify exact first-observation dates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock concept (magic-wavelength trapping of neutral atoms) and its realization achieved fractional uncertainty of order 1e-18, which has redefined the limits of time and frequency measurement and enables tests of fundamental physics, geodesy and a future redefinition of the second. It is a clear invention with immediate experimental verification.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice scheme and led its first realization; Ye made decisive advances in performance and in the entire experimental toolchain, reaching record accuracy. Two-person credit is clean, although the 2005 Hall-Hansch prize for frequency combs and other clock groups (NIST, PTB, SYRTE) are close neighbours in the story.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by multiple national laboratories, with intercomparisons established; the technology is mature but the redefinition of the second has not yet occurred, so practical culmination is still pending.
uncertainties: Overlap with earlier clock-related recognition in 2005 and ion-clock recognition in 2012.
Other contributors to lattice-clock performance are not covered.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, and the experimental demonstration in HgTe quantum wells, established a new topological classification of electronic matter with robust edge states. The theory is original and influential, and the original experiment confirmed the prediction, which satisfies my requirement for experimental verification.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the foundational theoretical proposal; Molenkamp's group delivered the original experimental observation of edge conduction in HgTe, based on the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal, whose authors are not in the supplied credit. This leaves a real unresolved attribution question; the three-name set is defensible but incomplete.
assessment.maturity: Experimentally confirmed in multiple systems, including 3D topological insulators observed by ARPES, and broadly mature, but the 2016 prize already recognised topological phase transitions, so the committee must consider overlap and relative novelty.
uncertainties: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe prediction) and Fu-Kane 3D work are outside the supplied names.
Overlap with 2016 topological Nobel Prize.
Practical impact is still prospective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum cascade laser is a genuine invention: a semiconductor laser whose wavelength is set by layer thickness rather than the bandgap, based on intersubband transitions engineered in heterostructures. It gave practical mid-infrared and terahertz sources used in spectroscopy, sensing and gas analysis. Originality, experimental verification (1994) and impact are all clear.
assessment.attribution: Capasso and Faist led the original proposal and demonstration at Bell Labs with co-authors (Sirtori, Sivco, Hutchinson), while Cho's molecular beam epitaxy growth was essential. Kazarinov and Suris proposed the superlattice amplification concept in 1971, which may complicate priority; this should be examined carefully. Choosing three names omits several colleagues.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature with commercial products and independent replication worldwide, so recognition is certainly not premature; it has been the subject of other major prizes.
uncertainties: The Kazarinov-Suris 1971 proposal and other Bell Labs co-authors complicate the allocation.
Whether the prize committee regards this as engineering over physics.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The IceCube detection in 2013 of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos, followed by the 2018 association of a neutrino with the blazar TXS 0506+056, opened a new window onto the high-energy universe. This is a clearly original, experimentally verified discovery enabled by a bold instrument, and a door that I would like to see followed up.
assessment.attribution: The result is a large collaboration achievement; Halzen conceived and led the project, and Karle and Spiering held leading roles in construction and analysis. The three-name proposal is a pragmatic choice, but a fair credit for a collaboration of hundreds is intrinsically difficult, and the committee historically hesitates about it.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in part by independent analyses and data samples, but the sources of the bulk of the flux remain largely unidentified, so the interpretation is still developing, and recognition may be somewhat early.
uncertainties: The source population of the diffuse flux is unresolved.
Collaboration credit and the three-person limit.
Whether the discovery should await more complete multi-messenger confirmation.
